claim: PKM2 displayed nuclear translocation in astrocytes of EAE mice at the onset phase, which sustained to the peak and chronic phases of the disease.
source: Initially, nuclear translocation of PKM2 was observed at the onset phase, which sustained to the peak and chronic phases of the disease.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence staining data showing PKM2 localization in astrocytes across different EAE disease phases.

claim: The expression level and nuclear ratio of PKM2 was elevated in different phases of EAE compared to control mice.
source: Compared to the cytoplasmic localization of PKM2 in control mice, the expression level and nuclear ratio of PKM2 was elevated in different phases of EAE (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis of immunofluorescence images showing increased PKM2 nuclear ratio and expression levels.

claim: Supernatants from MOG35-55-stimulated splenocytes isolated from EAE mice elicit a T-cell response in the acute stage of EAE.
source: Supernatant of MOG35-55-stimulated splenocytes isolated from EAE mice were previously shown to elicit a T-cell response in the acute stage of EAE and are frequently used as an in vitro autoimmune model to investigate MS and EAE pathophysiology (Chen et al., 2009; Du et al., 2019; Kozela et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies demonstrating this effect.

claim: MOGsup-stimulated astrocytes displayed significantly higher nuclear ratio and expression levels of PKM2 compared to non-treated control astrocytes.
source: Consistently, compared to non-treated control astrocytes, MOGsup-stimulated astrocytes displayed significantly higher nuclear ratio and expression levels of PKM2 (Figure 1C and D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data from in vitro astrocyte cultures.

claim: DASA-58 pretreatment effectively reduced the nuclear ratio of PKM2 in MOGsup stimulated astrocytes.
source: Pretreatment with DASA-58 effectively reduced the nuclear ratio of PKM2 in MOGsup stimulated astrocytes (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data showing reduced nuclear PKM2 upon DASA-58 treatment.

claim: MOGsup stimulation induced an increase in the glycolytic activity of astrocytes, as evidenced by glucose consumption and lactate production.
source: As expected, MOGsup stimulation, which mimics the autoimmune response in MS patients, induced an increase in the glycolytic activity of astrocytes, as evidenced by glucose consumption and lactate production.
evidence: Supported by biochemical assays measuring glucose consumption and lactate production.

claim: DASA-58 treatment significantly counteracted the MOGsup-induced increase in glycolytic activity of astrocytes.
source: However, these effects were significantly counteracted by DASA-58 treatment (Figure 2C).
evidence: Supported by glucose consumption and lactate production assay data.

claim: DASA-58 pretreatment significantly inhibited the upregulation of phosphorylated c-myc triggered by MOGsup stimulation.
source: Among these proteins, DASA-58 pretreatment significantly inhibited the upregulation of phosphorylated c-myc triggered by MOGsup stimulation, without any notable effect on the total level of PKM2 (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by western blotting data showing reduced phospho-c-myc levels.

claim: Treatment with 25 μM and 50 μM DASA-58 impaired the proliferation of astrocytes, with 50 μM showing better effect.
source: Figure 2E showed that treatment with 25 μM and 50 μM DASA-58 impaired the proliferation of astrocytes, and 50 μM owned better effect.
evidence: Supported by CCK-8 proliferation assay data.

claim: 50 μM DASA-58 mostly abrogated the MOGsup-induced astrocyte proliferation.
source: Additionally, EdU incorporation assays showed that 50 μM DASA-58 mostly abrogated the MOGsup-induced astrocyte proliferation (Figure 2F and G).
evidence: Supported by EdU incorporation assay data.

claim: DASA-58 pretreatment reduced the expression of inflammatory cytokines including IL-6, TNF-α, and iNOS in MOGsup-stimulated astrocytes.
source: In addition, DASA-58 pretreatment reduced the expression of inflammatory cytokines including IL-6, TNF-α, and iNOS in MOGsup-stimulated astrocytes (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data measuring cytokine expression.

claim: Abrogation of PKM2 nuclear transport can markedly decrease the proliferation and glycolysis of astrocytes.
source: From the above results, we can conclude that abrogation of PKM2 nuclear transport can markedly decrease the proliferation and glycolysis of astrocytes.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experimental results showing effects of DASA-58 on astrocyte proliferation and glycolysis.

claim: Nuclear PKM2 has been reported to interact with STAT3 and NF-κB.
source: As nuclear PKM2 has been reported to interact with STAT3 and NF-κB, which are dominant signaling pathways involved in orchestrating cell proliferation, inflammation and glycolysis, we were curious to investigate whether nuclear PKM2 regulates the activation of these two pathways.
evidence: Supported by references to previous literature on PKM2 interactions.

claim: MOGsup stimulation increased the phosphorylation of STAT3 and NF-κB pathways.
source: MOGsup stimulation increased the phosphorylation of STAT3 and NF-κB pathways.
evidence: Supported by western blotting and immunofluorescence data showing increased phosphorylation.

claim: DASA-58 pretreatment partially attenuated the phosphorylation of STAT3 and NF-κB pathways following MOGsup stimulation.
source: As expected, DASA-58 pretreatment partially attenuated the phosphorylation of STAT3 and NF-κB pathways following MOGsup stimulation (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence and western blotting data.

claim: DASA-58 affected the activation state of astrocytes, as evidenced by the reduced expression of GFAP.
source: DASA-58 also affected the activation state of astrocytes, as evidenced by the reduced expression of GFAP (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data showing reduced GFAP expression.

claim: Inhibiting PKM2 nuclear localization with DASA-58 suppressed the nuclear retention of p50/p65 and STAT3.
source: Western blotting assays showed that inhibiting PKM2 nuclear localization with DASA-58 suppressed the nuclear retention of p50/p65 and STAT3 (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: Supported by nuclear-cytoplasmic fractionation and western blotting data.

claim: Immunoprecipitation confirmed the endogenous binding between PKM2 and NF-κB subunits p50/65, as well as between PKM2 and STAT3.
source: The results confirmed the endogenous binding between PKM2 and NF-κB subunits p50/65, as well as between PKM2 and STAT3 (Figure 3E).
evidence: Supported by immunoprecipitation experimental data.

claim: Nuclear PKM2 interacts with p50/p65 and STAT3, favoring their nuclear retention and the sustained activation of NF-κB and STAT3 signaling pathways.
source: Therefore, nuclear PKM2 interacts with p50/p65 and STAT3, favoring their nuclear retention and the sustained activation of NF-κB and STAT3 signaling pathways.
evidence: Inferred from immunoprecipitation and fractionation data showing PKM2 interactions and effects on nuclear retention.

claim: Post-translational modifications, including ubiquitination, acetylation, sumoylation and phosphorylation are major mechanisms to regulate the process of PKM2 nuclear translocation.
source: With deepening of the research, amounting evidences support that post-translational modifications (PTMs), representing by ubiquitination, acetylation, sumoylation and phosphorylation are major mechanisms to regulate the process of PKM2 nuclear translocation.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge from literature.

claim: Several enzymes involved in glycolysis and gluconeogenesis including ENO1, ALDOA, MDH2, LDHA, and LDHC were identified to interact with PKM2.
source: Several enzymes involved in glycolysis and gluconeogenesis including ENO1, ALDOA, MDH2, LDHA, and LDHC were identified to be interacted with PKM2 (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by mass spectrometry data identifying PKM2-interacting proteins.

claim: The binding proteins of PKM2 are enriched in metabolic processes according to Gene Ontology analysis.
source: Analysis of biological processes according to Gene Ontology (GO) terms confirmed that the binding proteins of PKM2 are enriched in metabolic processes (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by bioinformatic analysis of mass spectrometry data.

claim: PKM2-interacting proteins were enriched in glycolysis, gluconeogenesis and NF-κB pathway according to KEGG and Wikipathway enrichment analysis.
source: Moreover, the results of KEGG and Wikipathway enrichment analysis indicate that PKM2-interacting proteins were enriched in glycolysis, gluconeogenesis and NF-κB pathway (Figure 4C and D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, D).
evidence: Supported by pathway enrichment analysis of mass spectrometry data.

claim: TRIM21 was identified as an E3 ligase that interacts with PKM2.
source: Amongst these potential interacting proteins, the most attracting one is TRIM21, an E3 ligase involved in the process of ubiquitination (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by mass spectrometry data identifying TRIM21 as a PKM2-interacting protein.

claim: Molecular docking revealed a strong binding affinity between PKM2 and TRIM21.
source: Molecular docking revealed a strong binding affinity between PKM2 and TRIM21 (Figure 4E, left).
evidence: Supported by computational molecular docking analysis.

claim: TRIM21 is predicted to bind to PKM2 via hydrogen bonds between the amino acids of the two molecules.
source: TRIM21 is predicted to bound to PKM2 via hydrogen bonds between the amino acids of the two molecules (Figure 4E, right).
evidence: Supported by molecular docking predictions showing specific amino acid interactions.

claim: Immunoprecipitation demonstrated the endogenous binding of PKM2 with TRIM21 in primary astrocytes.
source: By immunoprecipitation assays, we demonstrated the endogenous binding of PKM2 with TRIM21 in primary astrocytes (Figure 4F).
evidence: Supported by immunoprecipitation experimental data.

claim: Reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation with either Myc or Flag antibodies verified exogenous binding between PKM2 and TRIM21.
source: Reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation with either Myc or Flag antibodies verified exogenous binding between PKM2 and TRIM21 (Figure 4G and H).
evidence: Supported by co-immunoprecipitation experimental data using tagged proteins.

claim: The PRY-SPRY domain of TRIM21 is responsible for the interaction with PKM2.
source: The deletion of C-terminal PRY-SPRY domain abolished the binding between TRIM21 to PKM2, which indicated that PRY-SPRY domain of TRIM21 was responsible for the interaction with PKM2 (Figure 4I).
evidence: Supported by domain deletion experiments and immunoprecipitation data.

claim: The AB domain (44–388 amino acids) of PKM2 might interact with TRIM21.
source: However, the deletion of either N- or C-terminal of PKM2 did not affect the binding between TRIM21 to PKM2, indicating that AB domain (44–388 amino acids) of PKM2 might interact with TRIM21 (Figure 4J).
evidence: Inferred from domain deletion experiments showing that neither N- nor C-terminal deletion abolished binding.

claim: TRIM21 is a multifunctional E3 ubiquitin ligase that plays a crucial role in orchestrating diverse biological processes, including cell proliferation, antiviral responses, cell metabolism and inflammatory processes.
source: TRIM21 is a multifunctional E3 ubiquitin ligase that plays a crucial role in orchestrating diverse biological processes, including cell proliferation, antiviral responses, cell metabolism and inflammatory processes (Chen et al., 2022a).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature on TRIM21 functions.

claim: TRIM21 expression in astrocytes was relatively high compared to other cell types in EAE mice.
source: Compared to that in other cell types, TRIM21 expression in astrocytes was relatively high (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data.

claim: TRIM21 expression was augmented in astrocytes in both peak and chronic phases of EAE compared to control mice.
source: Most importantly, TRIM21 expression was augmented in astrocytes in both peak and chronic phases of EAE compared to that in control mice (Figure 5B–D).
evidence: Supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data analysis.

claim: Bioinformatic analysis of the GEO database (GSE136358) revealed significant elevation of TRIM21 expression in astrocytes at the onset, peak, and chronic phases of EAE disease.
source: Consistently, bioinformatic analysis of the GEO database (GSE136358) revealed significant elevation of TRIM21 expression in astrocytes at the onset, peak, and chronic phases of EAE disease (Figure 5E).
evidence: Supported by analysis of publicly available gene expression data.

claim: qPCR and western blotting analysis revealed dramatic increases in TRIM21 mRNA and protein expression in activated astrocytes compared to non-stimulated astrocytes.
source: Compared to those in non-stimulated astrocytes, qPCR and western blotting analysis revealed dramatic increases in TRIM21 mRNA and protein expression in activated astrocytes (Figure 5F and G).
evidence: Supported by qPCR and western blotting experimental data.

claim: Immunofluorescence staining demonstrated that TRIM21 expression was greater in astrocytes from EAE mice when compared with control mice.
source: Moreover, immunofluorescence staining further demonstrated that TRIM21 expression was greater in astrocytes from EAE mice when compared with control mice (Figure 5H).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence staining data.

claim: Overexpression of TRIM21 induced a robust increase in the nuclear ratio of PKM2.
source: Overexpression of TRIM21 induced a robust increase in the nuclear ratio of PKM2 (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by nuclear-cytoplasmic fractionation and western blotting data.

claim: Knockdown of TRIM21 led to a reduction in the nuclear ratio of PKM2.
source: In contrast, knockdown of TRIM21 led to a reduction in the nuclear ratio of PKM2 (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by nuclear-cytoplasmic fractionation and western blotting data.

claim: K63-linked ubiquitination of PKM2 was enhanced upon overexpression of TRIM21.
source: Immunoprecipitation implied that K63-linked ubiquitination of PKM2 was enhanced upon overexpression of TRIM21 (Figure 6C).
evidence: Supported by immunoprecipitation data using K63-ubiquitin specific antibodies.

claim: TRIM21 promoted K63-linked ubiquitination of PKM2 and facilitated its nuclear translocation in astrocytes.
source: Collectively, the data showed that TRIM21 promoted K63-linked ubiquitination of PKM2 and facilitated its nuclear translocation in astrocytes.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experiments showing TRIM21's effects on PKM2 ubiquitination and localization.

claim: The levels of phosphorylated STAT3 and p65 were significantly increased upon TRIM21 overexpression.
source: Our results showed that the levels of phosphorylated STAT3 and p65 were significantly increased upon TRIM21 overexpression (Figure 6D).
evidence: Supported by western blotting data showing increased phosphorylation.

claim: Overexpression of TRIM21 promoted the binding of PKM2 to c-myc, STAT3 and p50 subunit of NF-κB.
source: As shown in Figure 6E, overexpression of TRIM21 promoted the binding of PKM2 to c-myc, STAT3 and p50 subunit of NF-κB.
evidence: Supported by immunoprecipitation data.

claim: Overexpression of TRIM21 increased the nuclear accumulation of c-myc, STAT3 and p50/p65 subunits.
source: Notably, fractionation analysis revealed that overexpression of TRIM21 increased the nuclear accumulation of c-myc, STAT3 and p50/p65 subunits.
evidence: Supported by nuclear-cytoplasmic fractionation data.

claim: Pretreatment with DASA-58 diminished the nuclear retention of c-myc, STAT3 and p50/p65 subunits in TRIM21-overexpressing cells.
source: Conversely, pretreatment with DASA-58, which abrogated the nuclear translocation of PKM2, diminished the nuclear retention of the aforementioned transcription factors (Figure 6F).
evidence: Supported by nuclear-cytoplasmic fractionation data.

claim: TRIM21 overexpression increased the ratio of EdU positive cells.
source: As shown in Figure 6G, TRIM21 overexpression increased the ratio of EdU positive cells.
evidence: Supported by EdU incorporation assay data.

claim: The increase in astrocyte proliferation caused by TRIM21 upregulation was significantly antagonized by DASA-58 treatment.
source: However, the increase in astrocyte proliferation caused by TRIM21 upregulation was significantly antagonized by the DASA-58 treatment (Figure 6G).
evidence: Supported by EdU incorporation assay data.

claim: Upregulated TRIM21 promoted lactate production and glucose consumption, which were reversed by DASA-58.
source: Similarly, upregulated TRIM21 promoted lactate production and glucose consumption, which were reversed by DASA-58 (Figure 6H).
evidence: Supported by lactate production and glucose consumption assay data.

claim: Nuclear PKM2-mediated metabolic reprogramming is crucial for TRIM21-stimulated proliferation of astrocytes.
source: In summary, our results indicate that nuclear PKM2-mediated metabolic reprogramming is crucial for TRIM21-stimulated proliferation of astrocytes.
evidence: Inferred from experiments showing that DASA-58 reverses TRIM21-induced proliferation and glycolysis.

claim: shTRIM21 treatment suppressed disease severity of EAE.
source: As expected, shTRIM21 treatment suppressed disease severity of EAE.
evidence: Supported by clinical scoring data from EAE mice.

claim: At day 22 p.i., shTRIM21-treated group showed reduced disease scores compared to control groups.
source: At the end time point at day 22 p.i., shTRIM21-treated group showed reduced disease scores compared to control groups (Figure 7A).
evidence: Supported by clinical scoring data from EAE mice.

claim: Nuclear PKM2 in astrocytes was reduced in shTRIM21-treated group when compared to shVec-treated group.
source: Consistent with in vitro results, nuclear PKM2 in astrocytes was reduced in shTRIM21-treated group when compared to shVec-treated group (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence staining data from spinal cord sections.

claim: Inflammation and demyelination were less pronounced in shTRIM21-treated group.
source: As expected, inflammation and demyelination were less pronounced in shTRIM21-treated group (Figure 7B and C).
evidence: Supported by HE and LFB staining data from spinal cord sections.

claim: TRIM21 expression was reduced in astrocytes after intracerebroventricular injection of shTRIM21 lentivirus.
source: Staining for TRIM21 showed that TRIM21 expression was reduced in astrocytes after intracerebroventricular injection of shTRIM21 lentivirus (Figure 7D).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence staining data.

claim: Knockdown of TRIM21 in astrocytes significantly increased MBP positive areas, indicating inhibited demyelination.
source: Knockdown of TRIM21 in astrocytes significantly increased MBP positive areas, which indicated the inhibited demyelination in shTRIM21-treated group compared with control group (Figure 7E).
evidence: Supported by MBP immunofluorescence staining data.

claim: Knocking down TRIM21 in astrocytes decreased GFAP expression on spinal cord sections.
source: Knocking down TRIM21 in astrocytes decreased GFAP expression on spinal cord sections.
evidence: Supported by GFAP immunofluorescence staining data.

claim: The decrease of GFAP+ cell numbers was observed in both gray and white matter from shTRIM21-treated mice.
source: The decrease of GFAP+ cell numbers was observed in both gray and white matter from shTRIM21-treated mice (Figure 7F).
evidence: Supported by quantification of GFAP immunofluorescence staining.

claim: shTRIM21-treated group showed a significant decrease in IBA1 positive cells in both white matter and gray matter of spinal cord.
source: Control group showed a widespread activation, while shTRIM21-treated group showed a significant decrease in IBA1 positive cells in both white matter and gray matter of spinal cord (Figure 7G).
evidence: Supported by IBA1 immunofluorescence staining data.

claim: Intraperitoneal treatment with TEPP-46 at a dosage of 50 mg/kg every other day from day 0 to day 8 post-immunization resulted in decreased disease severity in EAE.
source: Intraperitoneal treatment with TEPP-46 at a dosage of 50 mg/kg every other day from day 0 to day 8 post-immunization with MOG35-55 resulted in decreased disease severity (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Supported by clinical scoring data from EAE mice.

claim: TEPP-46-treated mice exhibited reduced inflammation and demyelination.
source: TEPP-46-treated mice exhibited reduced inflammation and demyelination (Figure 7—figure supplement 2B–E).
evidence: Supported by HE, LFB, and immunofluorescence staining data.

claim: The activation of GFAP positive astrocytes and IBA1 positive microglia were correspondingly reduced in TEPP-46-treated mice.
source: The activation of GFAP positive astrocytes and IBA1 positive microglia were correspondingly reduced in TEPP-46-treated mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 2D and E).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence staining data.

claim: TRIM21 deficiency in astrocytes or prevention of PKM2 nuclear translocation substantially inhibited inflammation and myelin depletion in EAE mice.
source: Taken together, these results showed that TRIM21 deficiency in astrocytes or prevention of PKM2 nuclear translocation substantially inhibited inflammation and myelin depletion in EAE mice.
evidence: Inferred from multiple in vivo experiments showing effects of TRIM21 knockdown and TEPP-46 treatment.

claim: This study is the first to document the nuclear translocation of PKM2 in astrocytes of EAE.
source: To the best of our knowledge, this study is the first to document the nuclear translocation of PKM2 in astrocytes of EAE.
evidence: Based on the authors' assessment of existing literature.

claim: An increased expression of the E3 ubiquitin ligase TRIM21 was observed in astrocytes from EAE mice.
source: Furthermore, we clarified a ubiquitination-mediated regulation of PKM2 nuclear transport. Specifically, we observed an increased expression of the E3 ubiquitin ligase TRIM21 in astrocytes from EAE mice, which promotes the nuclear translocation of PKM2, thus enhancing astrocyte activation (Figure 8).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq, immunofluorescence, and western blotting data.

claim: TRIM21 promotes the nuclear translocation of PKM2, thus enhancing astrocyte activation.
source: Specifically, we observed an increased expression of the E3 ubiquitin ligase TRIM21 in astrocytes from EAE mice, which promotes the nuclear translocation of PKM2, thus enhancing astrocyte activation (Figure 8).
evidence: Supported by multiple in vitro and in vivo experiments showing TRIM21's effects on PKM2 localization and astrocyte function.

claim: Ubiquitin-mediated degradation of PKM2 has been reported.
source: Ubiquitin-mediated degradation of PKM2 has been reported.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge from literature.

claim: E3 ligase CHIP directly interacts with PKM2 and mediates its degradation in ovarian cancer.
source: Recently, in ovarian cancer, E3 ligase CHIP was shown to directly interact with PKM2 and mediate its degradation (Shang et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: TRIM family E3 ligase TRIM35 mediates the degradation of PKM2 in cardiomyocytes and breast cancer cells.
source: TRIM family E3 ligase TRIM35 was previously shown to mediate the degradation of PKM2 in cardiomyocytes and breast cancer cells (Lorenzana-Carrillo et al., 2022; Wu et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Laforin/malin E3 ligase-induced ubiquitination of PKM2 did not lead to its degradation but impaired its nuclear transport.
source: Although laforin/malin E3 ligase-induced ubiquitination of PKM2 did not lead to its degradation, ubiquitination in this case impaired its nuclear transport (Viana et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Ubiquitination, in addition to SUMOylation and phosphorylation, could induce the relocalization of PKM2 in the nucleus.
source: Different from these findings, it should be emphasized that our study adds to the current knowledge that ubiquitination, in addition to SUMOylation (Zhou et al., 2022) and phosphorylation (Yang et al., 2012), could induce the relocalization of PKM2 in the nucleus.
evidence: Based on the current study's findings in context of existing literature.

claim: Multiple key molecules involved in metabolism, immunity and inflammation have been recognized as substrates of TRIM21.
source: As a traditional E3 ubiquitin ligase, multiple key molecules involved in metabolism, immunity and inflammation have been recognized as substrates of TRIM21 (Chen et al., 2022b).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Glycolytic-related enzymes including PFK1, GLUT1 and glycolysis-related transcription factor HIF-1α were identified to be substrates of TRIM21.
source: Glycolytic-related enzymes including PFK1 (Tang et al., 2022), GLUT1 (Gu et al., 2022) and glycolysis-related transcription factor HIF-1α (Chen et al., 2021) were identified to be substrates of TRIM21, and TRIM21 mediated the ubiquitin-dependent degradation of these proteins, thereby inhibiting aerobic glycolysis.
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: TRIM21 mediated the ubiquitin-dependent degradation of PFK1, GLUT1, and HIF-1α, thereby inhibiting aerobic glycolysis.
source: Glycolytic-related enzymes including PFK1 (Tang et al., 2022), GLUT1 (Gu et al., 2022) and glycolysis-related transcription factor HIF-1α (Chen et al., 2021) were identified to be substrates of TRIM21, and TRIM21 mediated the ubiquitin-dependent degradation of these proteins, thereby inhibiting aerobic glycolysis.
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: TRIM21 promoted K63-linked ubiquitination of PKM2, the second common type of linkage that is typically not associated with protein degradation.
source: Here, we found that TRIM21 promoted K63-linked ubiquitination of PKM2, the second common type of linkage that is typically not associated with protein degradation.
evidence: Supported by immunoprecipitation data showing K63-ubiquitination.

claim: Nuclear translocation of PKM2 is related to the pathogenesis of diverse CNS diseases, such as Alzheimer's disease, ischemic stroke, glioblastoma, and spinal cord injury.
source: The growing body of literature shows that nuclear translocation of PKM2 are related to the pathogenesis of diverse CNS diseases, such as Alzheimer's disease, ischemic stroke, glioblastoma, and spinal cord injury (Dhanesha et al., 2022; Liang et al., 2016; Traxler et al., 2022; Zhang et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Upregulation of nuclear PKM2 in neutrophils has been observed in both human and mouse models of ischemic stroke.
source: Specifically, in ischemic stroke, upregulation of nuclear PKM2 in neutrophils has been observed in both human and mouse models.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge from literature.

claim: Application of ML-265 (TEPP-46) to inhibit nuclear translocation of PKM2 improved stroke outcomes.
source: Application of ML-265 (TEPP-46) to inhibit nuclear translocation of PKM2 improved stroke outcomes (Dhanesha et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: TEPP-46 has the ability to inhibit PKM2 nuclear translocation and glycolysis in CD4+ T cells.
source: Previous study demonstrated the ability of TEPP-46 in inhibiting PKM2 nuclear translocation and glycolysis in CD4+ T cells, and showed its therapeutic effect in limiting inflammation in EAE (Angiari et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: TEPP-46 showed therapeutic effect in limiting inflammation in EAE.
source: Previous study demonstrated the ability of TEPP-46 in inhibiting PKM2 nuclear translocation and glycolysis in CD4+ T cells, and showed its therapeutic effect in limiting inflammation in EAE (Angiari et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Glial cell activation and demyelination were inhibited following TEPP-treatment in EAE models.
source: Glial cell activation and demyelination were inhibited following TEPP-treatment in EAE models.
evidence: Supported by histological and immunofluorescence data from the current study.

claim: Astrocyte PKM2 nuclear translocation contributes to astrocyte glycolysis and activation.
source: Our findings reveal that astrocyte PKM2 nuclear translocation contributes to astrocyte glycolysis and activation, offering insights into PKM2's pivotal role in other astrocyte-associated CNS diseases.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experiments showing effects of PKM2 nuclear translocation on astrocyte function.

claim: Activated M1 microglial cells exhibit a metabolic switch toward aerobic glycolysis similar to that of astrocytes.
source: Activated M1 microglial cells exhibit a metabolic switch toward aerobic glycolysis similar to that of astrocytes.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: PKM2 is shown to interact with and phosphorylate STAT3 in cancer cells, immune cells and keratinocytes.
source: PKM2 is shown to interact with and phosphorylate STAT3 in cancer cells, immune cells and keratinocytes (Chen C. et al., 2022, Yang et al., 2023; Zhou et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: STAT3 positively regulates the expression of HIF-1α and MYC, two crucial promoters of Warburg effect.
source: STAT3 positively regulates the expression of HIF-1α and MYC, two crucial promoters of Warburg effect (Tošić and Frank, 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: STAT3 directly regulates the glycolysis-related genes by binding to the promoter of Slc2a1.
source: Moreover, STAT3 directly regulates the glycolysis-related genes by binding to the promoter of Slc2a1 (Li et al., 2022b).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: PKM2 interacts with and phosphorylates STAT3, thereby providing a rationale for the proliferation and enhanced glycolysis observed in astrocytes of EAE.
source: Aligning with these findings, our results reveal that PKM2 interacts with and phosphorylates STAT3, thereby providing a rationale for the proliferation and enhanced glycolysis observed in astrocytes of EAE.
evidence: Inferred from the current study's findings in context of existing knowledge about STAT3 function.

claim: p65-NF-κB interacts with PKM2.
source: Additionally, we also identified other transcriptional factors, such as p65-NF-κB, that interact with PKM2.
evidence: Supported by immunoprecipitation data from the current study.

claim: Blocking TRIM21 pathway effectively ameliorated disease severity of EAE, evidenced by reduced inflammation, demyelination, activation of astrocytes and microglia.
source: In the presented study, we showed that blocking TRIM21 pathway effectively ameliorated disease severity of EAE, which is evidenced by the reduced inflammation, demyelination, activation of astrocytes and microglia.
evidence: Supported by multiple in vivo experimental data including clinical scores, histology, and immunofluorescence.

claim: The in vivo effect of TRIM21 on promoting the nuclear translocation of PKM2 was verified by the observed inhibition of PKM2 nuclear immunostaining in astrocytes in shTRIM21-treated EAE mice.
source: Moreover, the in vivo effect of TRIM21 on promoting the nuclear translocation of PKM2 were verified, as evidenced by the observed inhibition of PKM2 nuclear immunostaining in astrocytes in shTRIM21-treated EAE mice.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data from spinal cord sections.

claim: Targeting TRIM21-PKM2 is a promising approach for clinical treatment of multiple sclerosis.
source: Our in vivo results suggested that targeting TRIM21-PKM2 is a promising approach for clinical treatment of multiple sclerosis.
evidence: Inferred from the therapeutic effects observed in EAE models.

claim: PKM2 nuclear translocation is the key mechanism accounting for glycolysis-dominant metabolic switch and proliferation of astrocytes.
source: In conclusion, our study revealed that PKM2 nuclear translocation is the key mechanism accounting for glycolysis-dominant metabolic switch and proliferation of astrocytes.
evidence: Inferred from multiple experiments showing effects of PKM2 nuclear translocation on astrocyte metabolism and proliferation.

claim: The study proposes a post-translational modification mechanism for the regulation of PKM2 nuclear translocation by the ubiquitin ligase TRIM21.
source: We propose a post-translational modification mechanism for the regulation of PKM2 nuclear translocation by the ubiquitin ligase TRIM21.
evidence: Based on the experimental findings showing TRIM21-mediated ubiquitination and nuclear translocation of PKM2.

claim: The study provides a rationale for targeting glycolysis metabolism to ameliorate astrocyte-mediated CNS diseases.
source: From the perspective of metabolism, our study provides a rationale for targeting glycolysis metabolism to ameliorate astrocyte-mediated CNS diseases.
evidence: Inferred from the therapeutic effects observed when targeting the TRIM21-PKM2 axis.

claim: EAE is widely used as a mouse model of multiple sclerosis.
source: EAE is widely used as a mouse model of multiple sclerosis, which is typically induced by active immunization with different myelin-derived antigens along with adjuvants such as pertussis toxin (PTX).
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about EAE as a model system.

claim: MOG 35-55 peptide is one widely used antigen for EAE induction.
source: One widely used antigen is the myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG) 35-55 peptide (Nitsch et al., 2021), which was adopted in our current studies.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature and established methodology.

claim: Reactive astrocytes play critical roles in the occurrence of various neurological diseases such as multiple sclerosis.
source: Reactive astrocytes play critical roles in the occurrence of various neurological diseases such as multiple sclerosis.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge from literature.

claim: Activation of astrocytes is often accompanied by a glycolysis-dominant metabolic switch.
source: Activation of astrocytes is often accompanied by a glycolysis-dominant metabolic switch.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge from literature.

claim: Prevention of PKM2 nuclear import by DASA-58 significantly reduced the activation of mice primary astrocytes, observed by decreased proliferation, glycolysis and secretion of inflammatory cytokines.
source: Prevention of PKM2 nuclear import by DASA-58 significantly reduced the activation of mice primary astrocytes, which was observed by decreased proliferation, glycolysis and secretion of inflammatory cytokines.
evidence: Supported by multiple experimental data including proliferation assays, glycolysis measurements, and cytokine expression analysis.

claim: TRIM21 interacted with PKM2, promoted its nuclear translocation and stimulated its nuclear activity to phosphorylate STAT3, NF-κB and interact with c-myc.
source: Most importantly, we identified the ubiquitination-mediated regulation of PKM2 nuclear import by ubiquitin ligase TRIM21. TRIM21 interacted with PKM2, promoted its nuclear translocation and stimulated its nuclear activity to phosphorylate STAT3, NF-κB and interact with c-myc.
evidence: Supported by immunoprecipitation, fractionation, and western blotting data.

claim: Single-cell RNA sequencing and immunofluorescence staining demonstrated that TRIM21 expression was upregulated in astrocytes of EAE.
source: Further single-cell RNA sequencing and immunofluorescence staining demonstrated that TRIM21 expression was upregulated in astrocytes of EAE.
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data and immunofluorescence staining.

claim: TRIM21 overexpressing in mice primary astrocytes enhanced PKM2-dependent glycolysis and proliferation, which could be reversed by DASA-58.
source: TRIM21 overexpressing in mice primary astrocytes enhanced PKM2-dependent glycolysis and proliferation, which could be reversed by DASA-58.
evidence: Supported by glycolysis assays and proliferation assays in TRIM21-overexpressing cells with and without DASA-58 treatment.

claim: Intracerebroventricular injection of a lentiviral vector to knockdown TRIM21 in astrocytes effectively decreased disease severity, CNS inflammation and demyelination in EAE.
source: Moreover, intracerebroventricular injection of a lentiviral vector to knockdown TRIM21 in astrocytes or intraperitoneal injection of TEPP-46, which inhibit the nuclear translocation of PKM2, effectively decreased disease severity, CNS inflammation and demyelination in EAE.
evidence: Supported by clinical scoring, histological analysis, and immunofluorescence data from EAE mice.

claim: Intraperitoneal injection of TEPP-46, which inhibits the nuclear translocation of PKM2, effectively decreased disease severity, CNS inflammation and demyelination in EAE.
source: Moreover, intracerebroventricular injection of a lentiviral vector to knockdown TRIM21 in astrocytes or intraperitoneal injection of TEPP-46, which inhibit the nuclear translocation of PKM2, effectively decreased disease severity, CNS inflammation and demyelination in EAE.
evidence: Supported by clinical scoring, histological analysis, and immunofluorescence data from EAE mice.

claim: Multiple sclerosis is a chronic inflammatory disease of the CNS, which accounts for the leading cause of neurological disability in young adults.
source: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic inflammatory disease of the CNS, which accounts for the leading cause of neurological disability in young adults.
evidence: Based on established medical knowledge about multiple sclerosis.

claim: The hallmarks of multiple sclerosis are varied and complex, ranging from astrocyte proliferation, microglia activation, neuroinflammation and damage to myelin sheaths.
source: The hallmarks of this disease is varied and complex, ranging from astrocyte proliferation, microglia activation, neuroinflammation and damage to myelin sheaths (Kuhlmann et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature and established medical knowledge.

claim: Local glia cells have been shown to potentiate inflammation and lead to neurodegeneration in MS.
source: However, with the deepening of research, local glia cells have been shown to potentiate inflammation and lead to neurodegeneration, among which astrocytes have attracted much attention with their diverse functions (Lee et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Astrocytes are the most abundant type of glia cells and provide physical, structural, and metabolic support for neurons.
source: Astrocytes are the most abundant type of glia cells and provide physical, structural, and metabolic support for neurons.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about astrocytes.

claim: Reactive astrocyte or astrogliosis results in loss of brain homeostatic functions and leads to the occurrence of neurological and neuropsychiatric disorders.
source: This phenomenon, also termed reactive astrocyte or astrogliosis, results in loss of brain homeostatic functions and leads to the occurrence of neurological and neuropsychiatric disorders (Verkhratsky et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The presence of activated astrocytes, evidenced by increased GFAP staining, was found before immune cell infiltration in MS and EAE.
source: The presence of activated astrocytes which is evidenced by increased GFAP staining, was found before immune cell infiltration in MS and its animal model, EAE (Correale and Farez, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Activated astrocytes are considered to be early events and contributors to lesion development in MS and EAE etiopathology.
source: Several lines of evidence bolster the conception that activated astrocytes are considered to be early events and contributors to lesion development in MS and EAE etiopathology (das Neves et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Proinflammatory immune cells, including reactive astrocytes, usually undergo a metabolic switch from oxidative phosphorylation to Warburg-type glucose metabolism.
source: Proinflammatory immune cells, including reactive astrocytes, usually undergo a metabolic switch from oxidative phosphorylation to Warburg-type glucose metabolism (Vaupel and Multhoff, 2021; Xiong et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Elevated level of aerobic glycolysis has been characterized in astrocytes of MS patients.
source: Moreover, elevated level of aerobic glycolysis has been characterized in astrocyte of MS patients (Afzal et al., 2020; Nijland et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Elevated glycolysis is crucial for sustaining astrocyte proliferation, the secretion of proinflammatory cytokines and neurotrophic factors and subsequent neuronal loss in the CNS.
source: Elevated glycolysis is crucial for sustaining astrocyte proliferation, the secretion of proinflammatory cytokines and neurotrophic factors and subsequent neuronal loss in the CNS.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about glycolysis in astrocytes.

claim: PKM2 is a rate-limiting enzyme of glycolysis and a key molecule that governs aerobic glycolysis.
source: Pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2), a rate-limiting enzyme of glycolysis, is a key molecule that governs aerobic glycolysis.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about PKM2.

claim: Low glycolytic enzyme activity of PKM2 promotes the conversion of pyruvate to lactate, which leads to aerobic glycolysis.
source: Low glycolytic enzyme activity of PKM2 promotes the conversion of pyruvate to lactate, which leads to aerobic glycolysis (Lee et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: In the cytoplasm, PKM2 exists in tetrameric form and possesses high pyruvate kinase activity.
source: In the cytoplasm, PKM2 exists in tetrameric form and possesses high pyruvate kinase activity.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about PKM2 structure and function.

claim: PKM2 can translocate to the nucleus in its dimeric form.
source: Specifically, PKM2 can translocate to the nucleus in its dimeric form.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about PKM2.

claim: Nuclear PKM2 can act as a protein kinase or transcriptional coactivator to regulate proliferation, inflammation, and metabolic reprogramming of cells.
source: With a low-glycolytic function, nuclear PKM2 can act as a protein kinase or transcriptional coactivator to regulate proliferation, inflammation, and metabolic reprogramming of cells (Liu et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The overexpression and nuclear translocation of PKM2 have been well documented in CNS disease.
source: The overexpression and nuclear translocation of PKM2 have been well documented in CNS disease.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge from literature.

claim: Nuclear PKM2 was upregulated in neutrophils and macrophages in patients with ischemic stroke.
source: Moreover, nuclear PKM2 was upregulated in neutrophils and macrophages in patients with ischemic stroke (Dhanesha et al., 2022; Li et al., 2022a).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Nuclear PKM2 in neurons was shown to promote neuronal loss in Alzheimer's disease.
source: Nuclear PKM2 in neurons was shown to promote neuronal loss in Alzheimer's disease (Traxler et al., 2022), suggesting that PKM2 is a key player in the development of neurological disease.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: PKM2 is a key player in the development of neurological disease.
source: Nuclear PKM2 in neurons was shown to promote neuronal loss in Alzheimer's disease (Traxler et al., 2022), suggesting that PKM2 is a key player in the development of neurological disease.
evidence: Inferred from multiple studies showing PKM2's role in various neurological diseases.

claim: Previous studies have suggested that PKM2 could regulate astrocyte proliferation.
source: Although previous studies have suggested that PKM2 could regulate astrocyte proliferation (Zhang et al., 2015), its potential function in astrocyte metabolic reprogramming and the upstream mechanisms underlying PKM2 nucleocytoplasmic shuttling are still elusive.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: TRIM21 belongs to the TRIM protein family which possess the E3 ubiquitin ligase activity.
source: TRIM21 belongs to the TRIM protein family which possess the E3 ubiquitin ligase activity.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about TRIM21.

claim: Emerging evidences have documented the multifaceted role of TRIM21 in cell cycle regulation, inflammation, and metabolism.
source: In addition to its well-recognized function in antiviral responses, emerging evidences have documented the multifaceted role of TRIM21 in cell cycle regulation, inflammation, and metabolism (Chen et al., 2022a).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The precise mechanisms underlying the involvement of TRIM21 in CNS diseases remain largely unexplored.
source: Nevertheless, the precise mechanisms underlying the involvement of TRIM21 in CNS diseases remain largely unexplored.
evidence: Based on assessment of existing literature.

claim: Targeting TRIM21-PKM2 axis may be a potential therapeutic strategy for the treatment of astrocyte-involved neurological disease.
source: Targeting this axis may be a potential therapeutic strategy for the treatment of astrocyte-involved neurological disease.
evidence: Inferred from the therapeutic effects observed in EAE models when targeting this pathway.
